conflict_topics: allocation of the single window corner in the living room
Agent A's permanent weekday desk vs Agent D's need for a prayer space
Agent B's guest seating on weekends
feasibility of schedules/packing up vs permanence
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants state concrete constraints (light for work, daily prayers, no-window for C's room, weekend guest seating) which grounds the disagreement.
Several practical proposals are offered (schedule, folding desk, help packing, clearing corner) but key feasibility constraints (A's complex hardware setup) repeatedly block settlement.
The conversation remains focused on the concrete resource issue and does not devolve into irrelevant topics or role confusion.
evaluation.final_reason: No affirmative agreement or accepted arrangement was reached by the end of the transcript. Multiple parties consistently asserted incompatible practical claims on the same corner (A: weekday desk that is hard to dismantle; D: daily prayer space; C: laundry drying; B: guest seating on weekends). The last move (Agent D proposing to clear the corner and try rearranging) is a constructive suggestion but was not accepted or turned into a concrete, mutually agreed plan within the transcript.
position_change_notes: Agent A remained firm that their workstation cannot be packed away weekly; no substantive concession from A.
Agent B moved from proposing schedule solutions to offering active help (pack/unpack) but that was refused; B also reasserted the normative claim that the living room is shared.
Agent C consistently advocated for the laundry-drying need and drew attention to practical constraints of moving the rack.
Agent D shifted from requesting the corner for prayers to proposing collective clearing and rearrangement — a move toward problem-solving but not an accepted change by others.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'I need to have my desk here...only place ... with enough light' vs Agent D: 'for my prayers, I need a clean space that's set aside...people won't be walking past.'
Agent A: notes Agent C's laundry rack is here too; Agent B: 'That corner is where my friends sit when they come over on weekends.' Multiple parties claim the same single corner.
Agent D: needs the space 'a few times every day' for prayer; Agent B: insists without the corner they can't have friends — conflicting, ongoing claims.
Agent C: 'My room doesn't have a window. It's the only place I can dry my clothes.' Agent D: summarizes that everyone needs the corner — conflict acknowledged but not resolved.

Agent A: 'My desk has to stay there...not something I can pack away every day. Maybe schedule around the desk.' Agent B: 'But if your desk is there permanently, there's no space for people to sit on weekends.'
Agent A: insists desk can't be packed away; Agent B: proposes 'Could you get a folding desk, then?' — suggested solution rejected implicitly by A's constraint.
Agent B offers to help pack/unpack on weekends; Agent A: rejects because setup (two monitors, wiring) takes long and isn't practical to tear down weekly.

Agent B: 'So that corner is your permanent office now?' Agent D: 'If the desk is there permanently, that means there's no space for my prayer mat either.' Tension increases over permanence and exclusion.

Agent A clarifies the desk 'has to be there every weekday' (not every day); Agent B: 'Nobody's saying you have to move it every day. Just for the weekends.' Narrowing of claims but the weekend conflict remains.

Agent A reiterates inability to move weekend setup; Agent B replies normatively: 'It's the living room... a shared space... can't just become one person's permanent office.' The normative claim reopens contest over rights to the shared space.
Agent C: 'If your desk is permanent, where does my laundry rack go?' Agent A: says rack is there now and not necessarily needing to move — another unresolved incompatibility about physical placement.

Agent C: asks where Agent D's things would go; Agent D: proposes 'try clearing the corner completely and then see how we can arrange things so everything fits.' Moves the conversation toward cooperative rearrangement but no agreement yet.

substantive_insights: A's technical workstation imposes a high switching cost that makes weekly teardown unrealistic, which is the main practical blocker to weekend-sharing proposals.
B's weekend use is inherently incompatible with any arrangement that treats the corner as permanently occupied on weekends.
C's laundry need is constrained by the lack of a window in their room, making relocation nontrivial.
D's need is recurring (multiple daily prayers) and value-based (requires a set-aside clean space), so simple temporal sharing may not satisfy it.
The final suggestion to clear and rearrange is a promising cooperative step but requires mutual buy-in and concrete roles to be a settlement.
